newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Johnson's Well finds W.Australia deposit.
newsitem.headline: Johnson's Well finds W.Australia deposit.

text.p: Gold miner Johnson's Well Mining NL said on Wednesday it had found a major new deposit in Western Australia state on tenements acquired through its joint venture with Aurora Gold Ltd and Delta Gold NL.

Joe Gutnick's Johnson's Well said in a statement the deposit was discovered at Rosemont in the Duketon Belt on tenements acquired though the joint venture with Aurora and Delta it announced on March 17.

The best results achieved to date included 29 metres at 23 grams per tonee gold from a depth of 109 metres, 55 metres at 6.3 g/t from 239 metres depth, 52 metres at 4.9 g/t from 238 metres depth and 62 metres at 3.2 g/t from 132 metres depth.
"The mineralisation which remains open along strike and at depth has been intersected over a strike length of 900 metres and to a vertical depth of 300 metres," Johnson's Well said in a statement.
The Rosemont find is between 20 and 60 metres wide and was find in the same structural corridor which contains Johnson Mining's Famous Blue mineralisation.
Intensive drilling was taking place so a mineral resource estimate could be completed during the September quarter, the company said.
Johnson's added a combined mineral resource estimate of 579,000 ounces of gold had been outlined at Famous Blue and Erlistoun, about 35 km and 15 km from Rosemont respectively.
